Use `twoPhaseEulerFoam` to simulate a steady-state two-phase oil-water flow in a horizontal pipe.
Set the pipe axis along the x direction.
Use a pipe diameter of 0.05 m and a pipe length of 2 m.
Generate the mesh with `blockMesh` using 80 cells axially and 16 cells in the cross-sectional direction.
Impose at the inlet a fixed mixture velocity of 1 m/s in the axial direction (`fixedValue uniform (1 0 0)`) for both phases.
Impose at the inlet `alpha.water = 0.3` with `fixedValue uniform 0.3`.
Use `noSlip` on the pipe walls for velocity.
Set the outlet `alpha.water` boundary condition to `zeroGradient`.
Set the outlet `p_rgh` boundary condition to `fixedValue uniform 0` and use `fixedFluxPressure` at the inlet.
Configure `ddtSchemes` with `default steadyState` in `system/fvSchemes` to achieve a true steady-state solution.
Use water as the continuous phase with density 1000 kg/m3 and kinematic viscosity 1e-06 m2/s.
Use oil as the dispersed phase with density 830 kg/m3 and kinematic viscosity 1e-05 m2/s.
Use the standard `kEpsilon` RAS turbulence model for both phases.
Use the `SchillerNaumann` drag model as the only interfacial interaction in `constant/phaseProperties`.
Run the case until the residuals converge to a steady solution.
Report the final phase distribution and pressure drop along the pipe.
